children: Grades were mixed on Tuesday, dealers said, after shipping sources said Saudi Arabia had suspended loadings at a key port while a report said a top U.S. Congress leader was open to exploring a diesel fuel ban.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he is “open to exploring” an export ban for diesel fuel as average national prices surge past $6 a gallon, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday.

Concerns over supply from the Middle East intensified after Saudi Arabia suspended loadings at Yanbu on its Red Sea coast following Friday's Houthi attacks on the kingdom's East-West pipeline, according to a Reuters report, citing sources. The port serves as a key alternative export outlet for Saudi crude. Riyadh has also informed European customers that some September-loading crude cargoes will be cancelled.

Prices for some physical oil cargoes in Europe jumped to more than $130 a barrel on Tuesday, approaching record highs reached in April, as buyers rush to find alternatives to disrupted Middle East energy supplies.
Mars, the benchmark U.S. sour crude grade favored by European refiners, rose by $1 to a midpoint premium of $5 a barrel to U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures.

The Brent-WTI spread narrowed to minus $7.89 a barrel in the latest trade, but remained well above the roughly $4 threshold that typically makes U.S. crude economically attractive to European refiners.
Light Louisiana Sweet for October delivery firmed 25 cents to a midpoint of a $5.25 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $4.50 and $6.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
Mars Sour rose $1 to a midpoint of a $5.00 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $4.80 and $5.20 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
WTI Midland fell 30 cents to a midpoint of a $1.50 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $1.30 and $1.70 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
West Texas Sour was unchanged at a midpoint of a 20-cent discount and was seen bid and offered between a​ discount of 40 cents and parity to U.S. crude futures
WTI at East Houston, also known as MEH, traded between a $1.80 and $2.20 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
rose $3.07 to settle at $108.75 a barrel on Tuesday​
futures rose $4.44 to settle at $105.83 a barrel
The Brent/WTI spread narrowed 65 cents to last trade at minus $7.89, after hitting a high of minus $7.54 and a low of minus $9.00.
